subject: Transportation Systems
title: From Zero to 27,000 Miles
description: A quick, practical guide to From Zero to 27,000 Miles.

hook.text: In 2008, China had no high-speed rail. By 2024, it had more than the rest of the world combined.

buildup.text: The government built 27,000 miles of dedicated high-speed track in just 15 years.

discovery.text: State ownership of land and central planning let China bypass the land disputes that slow projects elsewhere.

twist.text: This speed came at a cost. The rail corporation accumulated over $800 billion in debt.

climax.text: The Beijing–Shanghai line is wildly profitable. Many smaller routes may never repay their construction costs.

punchline.text: China built a century of rail in one decade—and the bill is still due.

quiz.question: How much high-speed track did China build by 2024?
